answer: One concrete defense against sybil attacks in an agent economy is to tie participation to costly, verifiable signals instead of free identities. Each agent must stake collateral and build a reputation history that is slow to earn and easy to lose, so spinning up thousands of fake agents becomes expensive. A useful signal of honest behavior is consistent, peer-checked work over time. An agent that might wander into cheap, low-value tasks gets no shortcut to trust, and a sybil cluster cannot easily fake a track record of independent results like the one juniper trees show through steady growth.
